title: He gave private tuitions to support his family. In 2026, Forbes put him on its billionaires list. October 30, 2026.
excerpt: From a physicist whose career pivot built both an institute and a nuclear program, to a diplomat's daughter now representing Britain at the Vatican, to a district that waited 80 years for its first train, to a tuition teacher turned billionaire edtech founder - October 30's four stories are about what one redirected career can eventually build.
bodyHtml:
Every story today traces back to a single turn in the road - an engineering student who switched to physics, a market-stall family whose daughter now represents a nation, a railway line that finally reached a place independence forgot, and a private tutor whose one-on-one lessons became a company serving millions.

October 30, 1909: a boy was born in Bombay who would found both India's top physics institute and its nuclear program

Homi Jehangir Bhabha, born into a Parsi family in Bombay, switched from mechanical engineering to physics at Cambridge, then founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research in 1945 and later the Atomic Energy Commission of India.

Her parents sold curtains from a market stall in Leicester. In 2026, their daughter became Britain's Ambassador to the Vatican

Tammy Sandhu, born in Leicester to parents who migrated from Punjab in the 1960s, presented her credentials to Pope Leo XIV on August 28, 2026, becoming the first woman of Indian origin to serve as the UK's Ambassador to the Holy See.

A Madhya Pradesh district just got its first railway line since Independence

Two new rail sections spanning 118 kilometres were inaugurated on October 24, 2026, finally connecting Sidhi district to India's railway network nearly 80 years after independence.

He gave private tuitions in Prayagraj to support his family. In 2026, Forbes put him on its billionaires list

Alakh Pandey built a YouTube physics-teaching channel from 2014, co-founded PhysicsWallah in 2020, and entered the Forbes World's Billionaires List in March 2026 following the company's November 2025 IPO.

Four stories, one pattern: a career pivot that built two institutions, a market stall's daughter now at the Vatican, a railway line eight decades overdue, and a private tutor whose classroom now has millions of students in it.
